# Spec-Driven Development (Full, Lightweight, Hotfix)

Methodology only: nothing here installs or runs an external SDD toolkit. Records follow the canonical sdd-project schema (`.claude/dac/sdd/`).

## Modes

### full

- Use when: New products, new capabilities, cross-cutting or high-risk work, anything touching data models, security or multiple components, or work whose requirements are not yet understood.
- Required phases: constitution, specify, clarify, plan, checklist, tasks, analyze, implement, converge, independent-validation
- Skippable phases: none
- Gates: pre-implementation, pre-migration, pre-production-mutation, pre-deployment, pass

### lightweight

- Use when: Well-understood, bounded changes in an existing project that already has a constitution and an established approach, with a small number of tasks.
- Required phases: specify, plan, tasks, implement, independent-validation
- Skippable phases: constitution, clarify, checklist, analyze, converge
- Gates: pre-implementation, pre-migration, pre-production-mutation, pre-deployment, pass
- Max tasks: 10

### hotfix

- Use when: Urgent, narrowly scoped correction of a defect in existing behavior. Never for migrations, production schema changes or new capabilities. Urgency never waives approval or independent validation.
- Required phases: specify, tasks, implement, independent-validation
- Skippable phases: constitution, clarify, plan, checklist, analyze, converge
- Gates: pre-implementation, pre-migration, pre-production-mutation, pre-deployment, pass
- Max tasks: 3
- Never for: migration, production-schema

## Phases

- constitution: Record the project principles and non-negotiable constraints that every later artifact must respect. Owners: repo-analyst.
- specify: State what is needed and why as testable requirements with acceptance criteria, without choosing a technology. Owners: technical-planner, prompt-engineer, site-analyst.
- clarify: Resolve every open question in the requirements before planning. Owners: repo-analyst, prompt-engineer, site-analyst.
- plan: Choose the technical approach and record each decision with its rationale and the requirements it serves. Owners: technical-planner.
- checklist: Check requirement quality and testability before tasks are cut. Owners: technical-planner, e2e-tester.
- tasks: Break the plan into owned tasks, each linked to requirements and acceptance criteria, with explicit paths. Owners: technical-planner.
- analyze: Read-only consistency analysis across requirements, decisions, tasks and scope before any change is made. Owners: repo-analyst, technical-planner.
- implement: Execute approved tasks by an implementer, inside the declared scope only. Owners: frontend-expert, backend-expert, kmp-expert, e2e-tester.
- converge: Reconcile the implementation with the requirements, decisions and tasks and close any drift. Owners: frontend-expert, backend-expert, kmp-expert, e2e-tester.
- independent-validation: A validator that implemented nothing verifies every acceptance criterion and records evidence. Local final gate. Owners: code-reviewer.

## Gates

- pre-implementation: blocks The implement phase and any file change. Requires human approval. Requires: requirements-complete, tasks-have-criteria, traceability-complete, required-phases-complete, scope-confined.
- pre-migration: blocks Any database or data migration, including its authoring in a runnable form. Requires human approval. Requires: pre-implementation-passed, rollback-plan-recorded.
- pre-production-mutation: blocks Any change to production data, production schema or production configuration. Requires human approval. Requires: pre-implementation-passed, rollback-plan-recorded.
- pre-deployment: blocks Any deployment or release. Requires human approval. Requires: pre-implementation-passed, independent-validation.
- pass: blocks Recording a PASS validation result. Requires: independent-validation, useful-evidence, all-criteria-covered, tasks-done.

## Ownership

- repo-analyst (analyst, never implements): constitution, clarify, analyze.
- technical-planner (planner, never implements): specify, plan, checklist, tasks, analyze.
- prompt-engineer (specifier, never implements): specify, clarify.
- site-analyst (analyst, never implements): specify, clarify.
- frontend-expert (implementer, may implement): implement, converge.
- backend-expert (implementer, may implement): implement, converge.
- kmp-expert (implementer, may implement): implement, converge.
- e2e-tester (implementer, may implement): checklist, implement, converge.
- code-reviewer (independent-validator, never implements): independent-validation.

The independent validator implements nothing and is the only agent eligible for the final gate. Urgency never waives approval or independent validation. A blocked gate or denied permission stops the work (BLOCKED); it is never routed to another executor.
